'''Edward Bormashenko''' ({{Langx|he|אדוארד בורמשנקו}}) is a professor of [[Materials science|Materials Science]] and the Head of the Laboratory of Interface Science of the [[Ariel University]] in Israel. He was born in 1962 in [[Kharkiv]], Ukraine and lives in Israel since 1997. He studied in the V. N. [[National University of Kharkiv|Karazin Kharkiv National University]]. His research is in the [[polymer science]] and [[surface science]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Physics of wetting : phenomena and applications of fluids on surfaces|last=Yu.|first=Bormashenko, Edward|date=2017|publisher=De Gruyter|isbn=978-3110444810|location=Berlin|oclc=1004545593}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Wetting of real surfaces|last=Yu.|first=Bormashenko, Edward|date=2019|publisher=De Gruyter|isbn=9783110581188|edition=2nd|location=Berlin|oclc=1065733789}}</ref> He accomplished his PhD (supervised by Professor M. L. Friedman) in Moscow Institute of Plastics in 1990.

His scientific interests include: [[Ultrahydrophobicity|superhydrophobicity]], superoleophobicity, creating of surfaces with prescribed properties, [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]]- and [[Ultraviolet|UV]]-treatment of surfaces, plasma treatment of seeds, [[liquid marbles]] and their self-propulsion, the Moses effect (magnetically inspired deformation of liquid surfaces). Professor Bormashenko is also active in [[quantitative linguistics]], [[Topology|topological]] problems of physics (exemplifications of the [[Hairy ball theorem|"hairy ball" theorem]]), advanced dimensional analysis (extensions of the [[Buckingham π theorem|Buckingham theorem]]), variational analysis of "free ends" physical problems, enabling application of the "[[Transversality (mathematics)|transversality]] conditions".

In 1987 Dr. Bormashenko studied the mechanisms of destruction of ultra-thin island films by highly charged high-energy particles.<ref>{{Cite Dr. Bormashenko in 2023-2025 worked on the development of applications of the graph theory in physics. In 2025 introduced a synchronization procedure for clocks based on the Einstein–Landauer framework.
Dr. Bormashenko is also known for his numerous philosophical essays (written in Russian language) in which he investigates the Jewish religious thought, Russian literature and scientific methodology.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://7i.7iskusstv.com/avtory/bormashenko/|title=Эдуард Бормашенко {{!}} СЕМЬ ИСКУССТВ|language=ru-RU|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref> The central motif of his work is seeking the truth in the post-modern time. Bormashenko was influenced by [[Merab Mamardashvili]] and [[:ru:Воронель, Александр Владимирович|Alexander Voronel]]. Professor Ed. Bormashenko is married and has four daughters.
